keyVerseText: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
rootMeaning: The name אׇהֳלִיבָמָה (ʼOhŏlîybâmâh) is derived from the Hebrew words אֹהֶל (ʼôhel), meaning 'tent' or 'dwelling,' and בָּמָה (bâmâh), meaning 'high place' or 'height.' Literally, it signifies 'tent of the high place,' which evokes imagery of a dwelling situated on an elevated or prominent location. This etymology suggests a sense of a conspicuous or significant habitation, possibly symbolizing a place of importance or sacredness beyond the simple notion of a personal name.
usageInScripture: The word אׇהֳלִיבָמָה appears eight times in Scripture, primarily as a proper name. It is consistently used to identify a person, either as the wife of Esau or as an Edomite chieftain. The top translations reflect this, with the majority rendering it as 'of Aholibamah' or simply 'Aholibamah,' indicating its function as a proper noun rather than a descriptive term. This consistency underscores its role as a personal identifier tied to lineage and tribal leadership within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אׇהֳלִיבָמָה as 'tent of the high place' enriches our grasp of biblical names as more than mere labels; they often carry theological or symbolic weight. As a wife of Esau and an Edomite chief, Aholibamah's name may reflect cultural or spiritual dimensions of her identity and heritage. From a Christian perspective, recognizing the significance of names rooted in sacred or elevated imagery reminds us that God’s providence extends even into the details of personal identity and history. It also points to the reality that God’s unfolding plan includes diverse peoples and leaders, whose names and stories contribute to the broader biblical tapestry.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 36:2 introduces Aholibamah as one of Esau's wives, stating, 'Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite.' Here, the use of אׇהֳלִיבָמָה not only identifies a key figure in Esau's family line but also highlights her distinct heritage. The name's meaning, 'tent of the high place,' subtly points to her notable background and the elevated status her family held, which contributes to understanding the complex interrelations and spiritual contexts within Esau’s lineage.
